correctness.rationale: Norm(P-J/(nm))2 is convex and invariant under D_n x S_m, whose edge orbits are exactly the cycle and within-fiber clique edges; averaging any feasible P gives a globally no-worse two-class P. Fourier diagonalization of C_n and clique constant/contrast decomposition gives ALL eigenvalues 1-a*delta_k and 1-mb-a*delta_k of multiplicity m-1. With b=(1-2a)/(m-1), SLEM is maximum of three affine lines L=1-alpha*a, H=(-1+2ma)/(m-1), U=1/(m-1)+a*(beta-2m/(m-1)). For m2 even graph bipartite implies eigenvalue -1 for any no-holding P; m2 odd unique two-class line intersection. For m>=3 L falls, H rises, U nondecreases; first L/U or L/H crossing minimizes, except n=m=3 plateau. Algebra reduces odd-n crossover to m>=4(1+cos(pi/n)), lying strictly (7,8) for odd n>=5; n3 exactly6. Independent grid checked 35 n and 17 m and threshold. Analytical spectral/averaging proof, not finite grid, establishes arbitrary n,m.

value.rationale: Cyclic clique networks are a natural graph family for spatial/layered random walks, and forbidding all holding probabilities materially changes the mixing optimum. A global (not merely symmetric-edge-assumed) exact SLEM and sharp m7/8 eigenmode change give a useful graph-design phase diagram, including bipartite obstruction and scaling gain.

final_claim: For n>=3,m>=2, all real symmetric zero-diagonal stochastic edge-supported transitions on C_n square K_m minimize SLEM at a homogeneous two-edge-class transition. Complete exact optimum includes m2 even bipartite obstruction mu=1; m2 odd a=2/(4+gamma), mu=(4-gamma)/(4+gamma); m>=3 a*=min(aL,aH), mu=1-alpha*a*, aL=(m-2)/((m-1)(alpha+beta)-2m), aH=m/(2m+(m-1)alpha), with n=m=3 flat interval. For odd n>=5 low/high modes switch between m=7 and m=8, and fixed-m gap ~2pi²/n².
limitations: Zero-holding real symmetric P only; unique two-class optimality except special plateau, no uniqueness for unrestricted edge matrices; SLEM not exact total-variation mixing time.
